subject: Game Theory
title: The Shadow of the Future
description: A 60-second lesson on The Shadow of the Future.

hook.text: If you'll never see someone again, cheating tempts. If you'll meet tomorrow, you think twice.

buildup.text: Economists call this the 'discount factor'—how much you value future payoffs versus today's.

discovery.text: When future interactions matter enough, cooperation becomes self-enforcing. Cheating costs too much.

twist.text: But if the future feels distant or uncertain, the shadow weakens and defection creeps back.

climax.text: Online marketplaces create artificial shadows: ratings, reviews, and repeat-business incentives.

punchline.text: The future is the best enforcer of trust.

quiz.question: What is the 'shadow of the future'?
options: How much future interactions matter to current decisions
